notes: Reviewed every assigned file from start to finish. The two large generated precomputation sources were additionally checked line-by-line for table structure: 16,384 and 1,760 data entries respectively, each with exactly sixteen valid storage limbs; their consuming tests independently check on-curve membership, table progression, generators, and cross-algorithm multiplication results.

Closed the scratch-header addition as a negative control: src/scratch_impl.h:13-22 does not guard base_alloc + size against size_t wrap, but both the allocator and its secp256k1.c wrapper are static, and repository-wide call-site search found only tests, exhaustive tests, and a benchmark using fixed or internally bounded sizes. The public scratch-space API has been removed, so no hostile serialized input or supported public caller reaches an attacker-controlled size.

Closed scalar_mul_shift_var bounds as a negative control: both production backends rely on VERIFY_CHECK for the shift domain, but the functions are static and their only production call sites pass the compile-time constant 384.

Public parsing and mutation paths reject malformed serialized data and clear failure outputs as tested. Invalid pointers, undersized fixed buffers, overlapping or forged opaque objects, and caller-installed callbacks remain documented trusted programming-contract boundaries under the scan policy.
No raw-candidates artifact was created because no technically plausible source-to-sink candidate crossed the resolved threat boundary.
